title: Frontend wiring for backend-driven file processing (upload → process → download)

requirements.summary: Replace the placeholder useProcessFile mutation with a real backend-driven processing flow supporting tool selection, parameters, progress, and returning bytes + filename + contentType.
acceptanceCriteria: useProcessFile no longer throws the placeholder error and instead performs a real backend call sequence.
Upload progress updates the existing progress UI in tool pages that use a Progress component (e.g., PDF→Word, Image Compressor).
On success, the hook returns processedBytes + filename + contentType that can be downloaded via existing download helpers.

file_operations.description: Replace the placeholder mutation with a backend call sequence driven by an explicit operation selector and parameters. Use the blob-storage component's ExternalBlob (from the generated frontend bindings) to upload file bytes with progress (ExternalBlob.withUploadProgress) and to support large-file-compatible workflows. Normalize thrown backend/transport errors via normalizeBackendError as today. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add shared frontend types and helpers for tool processing: operation identifiers (at least pdf-to-word, image-compressor, image-resize-compress), parameter typing (targetWidth/targetHeight/maintainAspectRatio/format/quality), and lightweight client-side validation/mapping used by useProcessFile and tool pages to keep parameters consistent.

Update the frontend backend interface typings to include the backend functions required by useProcessFile for initiating an operation, uploading/attaching bytes (or ExternalBlob references), triggering processing, and retrieving the processed bytes + metadata (filename, contentType), along with structured errors. Keep the changes aligned with the actual candid-generated API once backend work is complete.

requirements.summary: Update the PDF→Word, Image Compressor, and Image Resize & Compress tool pages to run end-to-end via backend processing (upload → process → download) with correct filenames/content types and accurate privacy wording.
acceptanceCriteria: PDF to Word: uploading a PDF and clicking convert results in a downloadable .docx file that opens in Word/Google Docs.
Image Compressor: uploading an image and clicking compress results in a downloadable processed image with the expected (compressed) size change in typical cases.
Image Resize & Compress: processing uses the selected width/height/format/quality settings and downloads the resulting file with the correct extension and content type.
Any privacy/security FAQ or note that currently states processing is "entirely in your browser" is updated to accurate English text consistent with backend processing.
Errors from the backend display in the existing Alert UI with a user-friendly message.

file_operations.description: Switch the convert action to call useProcessFile with operation 'pdf-to-word' and use the returned filename and contentType when downloading (remove hardcoded DOCX content type). Ensure progress messaging reflects upload vs processing states based on mutation/progress callbacks, and keep backend errors surfaced through the existing destructive Alert.

Switch the compress action to call useProcessFile with operation 'image-compressor' and use the returned filename and contentType when downloading (stop deriving from the original file type). Preserve the existing preview, Progress UI, and error Alert behavior while relying on backend outputs.

Replace the current client-side resizeAndCompressImage canvas flow with backend-driven processing via useProcessFile using operation 'image-resize-compress' and passing the page’s current settings (targetWidth, targetHeight, maintainAspectRatio, format, quality). Update the UI state to show upload/progress/ready states using the existing Alert UI for errors and the existing Download button to download returned bytes using returned filename/contentType. Update any FAQ text that claims processing is entirely in-browser to accurate backend-processing wording.
